scenario: Select a story prompt for a child; user wants a curious protagonist rather than a brave one.
mechanism: Shift character motivation without implying fearlessness.

scenario: Explain the difference between 'listen' and 'hear'; user asks for a natural example involving a conversation.
mechanism: Contrast attention and perception without treating either as proof of understanding.

scenario: Plan a fictional puppet show with an offstage narrator; discuss puppets and scenery before drafting the opening.
mechanism: Keep the narrator offstage after two intervening exchanges.

scenario: Discuss a new routine that feels lonely; user clarifies they value solitude but miss occasional contact.
mechanism: Avoid treating solitude and companionship as opposites.

scenario: Arrange a set of fictional scene cards; user moves the final scene earlier but wants the others in their existing relative order.
mechanism: Apply a single move without reshuffling unrelated scenes.

scenario: Choose a way to keep track of ideas; user prefers voice notes but does not want transcription.
mechanism: Suggest an audio organization approach without claiming to record anything.

scenario: Interpret a supplied sentence 'I suppose so'; user clarifies it was said jokingly.
mechanism: Reconsider tone while avoiding certainty about enthusiasm.

scenario: Plan a fictional art exhibit with no labels on the works; discuss room layout and lighting before explaining how visitors identify pieces.
mechanism: Retain the label restriction after two exchanges and propose a separate guide only as an option.

scenario: Reflect on receiving criticism; user clarifies the content was useful but the public setting was uncomfortable.
mechanism: Separate substance from delivery.

scenario: Create a playful fictional recipe for a cloud; user changes the audience from young children to adults who enjoy absurd humor.
mechanism: Adjust language and humor without presenting the recipe as real.

scenario: Choose a way to keep an entryway clear; user clarifies the shared umbrella stand must stay.
mechanism: Work around the fixed shared item.

scenario: Discuss 'fair' in a fictional game; user asks whether equal turns always produce equal opportunity.
mechanism: Distinguish equal treatment from situational access without claiming a single rule.

scenario: Develop a fictional character who understands a language but does not speak it; discuss a visitor and setting before drafting their exchange.
mechanism: Preserve receptive but not spoken ability after two exchanges.

scenario: Discuss organizing a shared photo selection; user clarifies they can suggest choices but cannot decide for the group.
mechanism: Avoid implying final authority or consent from others.

scenario: Plan a paper chain decoration; user changes from alternating colors to a repeating pattern of their own description.
mechanism: Follow the supplied sequence without guessing missing elements.

scenario: Brainstorm a quiet way to celebrate finishing a personal project; user says they prefer recognition from themselves, not a gathering.
mechanism: Shift from social celebration to private acknowledgment.

scenario: Interpret a supplied dialogue where one speaker says 'that's one way to do it'; user adds that their tone was approving.
mechanism: Avoid assuming sarcasm from wording alone.

scenario: Plan an imaginary house tour where the upstairs is private; discuss the garden and kitchen before a visitor asks to explore.
mechanism: Respect the private area after two exchanges without inventing permission.

scenario: Discuss a family member's suggestion to keep a keepsake; user clarifies it belongs to the user and they are undecided.
mechanism: Support deliberation without treating advice as an obligation.

scenario: Co-write a fictional argument between two friends over a shared project; user decides both misunderstood the same vague instruction.
mechanism: Ground the conflict in ambiguity rather than malice.
